messages:
jamie: quick check-in: we need a deterministic sampling key for traces so sampled subsets are stable across components (router -> edge -> async ingest). proposal below.
noor: yes please. current randomness makes cost attribution a nightmare for billing windows.
lin: curious how this ties to tenant attribution vs feature-level cost. do we need two keys?
jamie: thinking two compact headers: rd-key (stable identity for tenant+org) and rd-shard (deterministic sample key). both tiny, both utf8-safe. example: rd-key: acct:ACCT42;svc:chat rd-shard: h:sha1:hexprefix
noor: rd-shard as hashed namespace makes it easy: router does hash(rd-key) xor ctrl-salt and mod 10000 to pick sample cohort buckets. reproducible everywhere.
lin: +1 for salt controlled at infra level so we can rotate without changing ingestion code. need to surface salt rotation plan and backfill semantics.
jamie: salt rotation plan: salt version in rd-shard header e.g. h1:sha1:abcd... so downstream can re-evaluate if needed; analytics should persist raw rd-shard value too for retrofitting.
devops-bot: infra: rollout note: edge-proxy 2.9.0 will inject rd-key when SDK absent; canary 5% tomorrow 02:00 UTC.
noor: what about partial sampling & rehydration? some downstream async pipelines only see a subset; if we sample early we lose coverage. maybe implement two-stage sampling: early minimal sampling (heavy path) and late enrichment sampling for analytics.
lin: two-stage makes sense. early stage uses rd-shard to decide route: hot path vs cold path. cold path writes full event to low-cost storage but marks sampled=false. late stage can promote some cold samples into analytics if rd-shard mod policy picks them.
jamie: exactly. important: cost attribution must attach rd-cost-key (a short canonical cost bucket id) to both hot and cold paths so billing reports reconcile. rd-cost-key should be stable and derived from org+feature mapping service.
noor: mapping service -> heavy. prefer caching at edge and using signed short token rd-cost to avoid lookups on every request. token contains encoded cost-bucket id + TTL, HMAC-signed by mapping service.
lin: signed token approach is neat. then ingest can verify signature and decode cheaply. token length ~ 20-32 bytes base64. watch proxies again.
jamie: followups: 1) header names and max lengths, 2) rd-shard hash algo and salt rotation, 3) rd-cost token format/HMAC algo, 4) two-stage sampling semantics doc. i'll draft RFC after we land on these.
noor: i'll prototype mapping service token issuer + verification code; will measure RPS/latency.
lin: i'll write sampling semantics doc and some example queries showing how to reconcile billing windows when early/late sampled.
jamie: ops question: if token verification fails at ingest, what's fallback? prefer to mark cost_unknown and route to conservative billing bucket to avoid undercharging. agreed?
devops-bot: alert rule: ingestion.cost_unknown spikes > 0.5% -> page oncall.
noor: agreed on conservative fallback (cost_unknown => bucket=shared_default). also emit enrichment_miss span tag.
jamie: last note: analytics/backfill: keep alias table for old-style tenant ids for 90 days, and store raw rd-key in raw-events for 7 days to allow re-eval. we can't backfill indefinitely.
lin: thumbs up. will include alias/backfill window in RFC.
rfc-bot: RFC template -> /docs/rfcs. tag rfc-obsv-sample-key. suggested filename 4624010000-det-sample-keys-and-cost-tokens.json
jamie: thanks all. i'll post the RFC 4624010000-det-sample-keys-and-cost-tokens.json tomorrow and ping reviewers. :rocket:
